record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.original_question: If M is an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension, must its universal cover M̃ be det-L²-acyclic and satisfy (-1)^((dim(M)-1)/2) * ρ^(2)(M̃) >= 0? If M is a closed connected Riemannian manifold of odd dimension with negative sectional curvature, must the same quantity be strictly positive? If M is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, must M̃ be det-L²-acyclic and satisfy ρ^(2)(M̃) = 0?

evidence.quote:
If M is an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension, then M̃ is det-L2-acyclic and
(−1)(dim(M)−1)/2 · ρ(2)(M̃) ≥ 0.

If M is a closed connected Riemannian manifold of odd dimension with negative sectional curvature, then M̃ is det-L2-acyclic and
(−1)(dim(M)−1)/2 · ρ(2)(M̃) > 0.

If M is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, then M̃ is det-L2-acyclic and
ρ(2)(M̃) = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed connected manifold with universal covering $\widetilde{M}\to M$, on which the fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$ acts freely. Recall that $M$ is called aspherical if its universal covering is contractible. The universal covering carries an equivariant $L^2$-de Rham (or cellular) complex of Hilbert $\mathcal{N}(\pi_1(M))$-modules; $\widetilde{M}$ is called det-$L^2$-acyclic if all its $L^2$-Betti numbers vanish and all Laplacians on the cellular $L^2$-chain complex have positive Fuglede–Kadison determinant in the sense of the group von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{N}(\pi_1(M))$. When $\widetilde{M}$ is det-$L^2$-acyclic, its $L^2$-torsion $\rho^{(2)}(\widetilde{M})\in\mathbb{R}$ is defined as the alternating sum of logarithms of these Fuglede–Kadison determinants (and is independent of CW-structure or Riemannian metric for aspherical $M$).

Prove or disprove each of the following statements.

(a) If $M$ is an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension, then $\widetilde{M}$ is det-$L^2$-acyclic and
$$(-1)^{(\dim M-1)/2}\,\rho^{(2)}(\widetilde{M}) \;\ge\; 0.$$

(b) If $M$ is a closed connected Riemannian manifold of odd dimension with negative sectional curvature, then $\widetilde{M}$ is det-$L^2$-acyclic and
$$(-1)^{(\dim M-1)/2}\,\rho^{(2)}(\widetilde{M}) \;>\; 0.$$

(c) If $M$ is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$ contains an infinite amenable normal subgroup, then $\widetilde{M}$ is det-$L^2$-acyclic and
$$\rho^{(2)}(\widetilde{M}) \;=\; 0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: These statements form Lück's L²-torsion conjecture (often called the L²-torsion sign / vanishing conjecture) for aspherical closed manifolds. The negatively curved Riemannian case (b) is known for hyperbolic manifolds of odd dimension via work of Lott, Lück, and Hess–Schick, where the L²-torsion is proportional to hyperbolic volume with nonzero constant in low odd dimensions and is known in general for hyperbolic manifolds. However, the general statements (a) and (c) for arbitrary aspherical closed manifolds remain open as of recent surveys on L²-torsion.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds (Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists these as open conjectures concerning det-L²-acyclicity and the sign/vanishing of ρ^{(2)} for aspherical closed odd-dimensional manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The three statements are stated as open conjectures.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on L²-torsion (Lück, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys current status of L²-torsion conjectures, including the parity/sign conjecture for aspherical odd-dimensional manifolds; results known for hyperbolic manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolic (negatively curved) case largely established; general aspherical case remains open.

status_evidence.title: L²-torsion of hyperbolic manifolds of finite volume
status_evidence.snippet: Proves nonvanishing of L²-torsion for odd-dimensional hyperbolic manifolds with the correct sign.
